normalized.answer: Exact words compared: the normative sentence is identical; the differences are curly vs straight quotes around "someFactoryMethodName"/"FactoryObject" and a transcription backslash after aFactoryObject, all inside the NOTE. No change in requirement; GR-16.2.2.2-1 is the right pointer.

definition-changed.answer: The rule's 'class of the object' is the object-orientation sense (§2002:4 4.33 = §2023:3.32), not class of a data item. Scope unchanged.

definition-dropped.answer: 2002 4.121 method matches 2023 9.3.4 (procedural entity of a class); FactoryObject is the same BASE instance method in both. No change.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:9.3.5 binds by method-name alone; 2023 9.3.6 requires 'an exact match between the method invocation and the method resolution signature' (overloading). FactoryObject takes no parameters and returns one object reference, so name binding and exact-match binding pick the same method; pb1548_standard_class_base matches its golden at --std 2002. No change.
